standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, Lemma divisors-lemma-characterize-OD and Remark divisors-remark-ses-regular-section; Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the sequence 0 -> O_X -> L -> L|_D -> 0 for the zero divisor D of a section, with deg(D) = deg(L) = d.

standard_prerequisites.name: Ampleness and vanishing on curves
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-ample-curve; Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma coherent-lemma-coherent-proper-ample
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the power L^tensor n with vanishing H^1 used to close the equality case.

core_obligations: Inequality (proof lines 667-689): assume V = H^0(X, L); the zero scheme D of a nonzero section is an effective Cartier divisor with L = O_X(D), deg D = d, and L|_D trivial, so dim H^0(D, L|_D) = d; the injection H^0(O_X) = 1 plus dim H^0(L) = r + 1 into the sequence gives r + 1 <= 1 + d.
Equality setup (proof lines 692-700): equality makes H^0(L) -> H^0(L|_D) surjective; the obstacle is the unknown H^1(X, L), and the strategy is to replace L by a power with vanishing H^1.

Doubling step (proof lines 702-720): a section t trivializing L|_D makes mu(H^0(L) tensor t) surject onto H^0(L^tensor 2|_D), so dim H^0(L^tensor 2) = r + 1 + d = 2r + 1 = deg(L^tensor 2) + 1; the same property propagates to L^tensor 2.
Conclusion (proof lines 722-735): L is ample, so H^1(L^tensor n) = 0 for n >= n_0; applying the equality argument to L^tensor n with n = 2^m large gives H^1(X, O_X) = 0, i.e. genus 0.
proof_roadmap: From a section of the linear system, form the Cartier divisor sequence and count dimensions to get r <= d.
In the equality case, identify the missing vanishing and plan to replace L by a large power.
Prove the doubling step: the tensor square inherits the dimension-equals-degree-plus-one property.
Use ampleness for a power with H^1 = 0 and run the equality argument on it to conclude genus 0.
difficulty_reason: The lemma bounds linear systems on a curve by their degree (statement lines 659-665). The proof (lines 667-735) does real work in both directions: the inequality comes from the section-sequence dimension count with the triviality of L|_D, and the equality case needs a genuine trick, replacing L by its tensor powers via a doubling argument that propagates the dimension identity to L^tensor 2 and then to a high power with vanishing H^1 furnished by ampleness. H2: compact and standard, but the doubling propagation is a real step.
